sources: Shiva Purana, Rudra Samhita, Kumara Khanda (Parvati fashions a boy and sets him to guard her door; Shiva is refused entry and the boy is killed in the fight; Parvati’s grief and anger; Shiva’s attendants, the ganas, bring an elephant’s head; Shiva restores the boy and makes him chief of the ganas, to be worshipped first)
The film’s note: versions appear in the Shiva Purana and other Puranas; details differ by region
Gajanana, a name of Ganesha: gaja (elephant) + anana (face)
check: The film says Parvati made the boy “from turmeric paste.” The Shiva Purana says from the dirt or unguent of her body; turmeric paste is the popular telling. Confirm this wording is fine.
The film softens the beheading to “a terrible misunderstanding at the door”; the lesson keeps it that gentle. Confirm acceptable.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? has something broken that you can’t put back the way it was? a plan, a friendship, your idea of how life would go.
options: then this story is for you. listen.
then you may already know what it became. listen.
good. keep this one for when it does.

steps.line: Parvati made a boy from turmeric paste, and breathed life into him.

steps.q: Parvati gives the boy his very first job. What do you think it is?
o: Guard her door and let no one in
steps.why: Guard the door. And he takes the job very seriously. Watch.

steps.line: Guard my door, she said, and let no one in.
Then Shiva came home. Neither knew who the other was, and there was a terrible misunderstanding at the door.

steps.q: In the Shiva Purana, Parvati had a reason for making the boy. What did she want?
o: A playmate while Shiva was away
A guard who answered to her alone
steps.why: All the household guards answered to Shiva, who walked in even while she bathed. So she made one who was hers. That’s why the boy wouldn’t budge.

steps.line: Parvati’s grief shook the whole universe. Shiva, heartbroken, set out to make it right.

steps.q: Shiva sends his followers out to find a new head. What instruction do many tellings say he gives?
o: Bring the bravest beast in the forest
Bring the first creature you meet
steps.why: The first one they met was an elephant. Nobody chose that face; it found him.

steps.line: His followers came back with an elephant’s head. Shiva gave the boy new life, and a promise: from now on, you will be honored first.

steps.pre: Ganesha is honored first, as Vighnaharta: the remover of
steps.why: Obstacles, vighna. Many tellings add that he can also place them in the path of the proud, so you greet him before you begin.

steps.line: Something broken can become something new, and even better.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Many Hindus read meaning into the elephant head. What do the big ears often stand for?
steps.why: Big ears to listen more, a small mouth to speak less: a common Hindu reading. The broken day gave him a face for wisdom.

say: here’s what i love. the elephant head was never the plan. and it became one of the most loved faces in hinduism.
in this story, a broken thing doesn’t go back to how it was. it becomes something new, and honored first. that’s why so many hindus remember ganesha before any new beginning.

steps.q: Shiva caused the harm. What makes the way he answered it worth honoring?
o: He proved who was in charge
He set it right, and then some
He said it was no one’s fault
steps.why: He didn’t stop at sorry: new life, a new face, first place, and leader of his own followers, which is what Ganapati means.

today.say: think of one thing in your life that broke. don’t ask how to glue it back. ask: what could this become? then make one small new start, and pause first, the way many hindus pause for ganesha. you can say “om gam ganapataye namah,” or just take a breath. it’s your choice.
options: then hold it gently. broken can become beloved.
that’s okay. the question will keep.
